summary: P0 cleanup + P1 session-persistence regression test. Backend: 79/79 existing tests pass. New cleanup suite (44 tests) — 43 pass, 1 fail. Critical bug found: POST /api/auth/logout ignores Authorization Bearer token (only reads session_token cookie), so frontend (which uses Bearer header) cannot actually invalidate sessions. Verified P0: /api/status GET+POST return 404, ADMIN_PASSWORD loaded from .env (no hardcoded fallback works). Verified P1: session token survives backend restart (MongoDB-backed admin_sessions collection). Frontend: desktop nav links + new mobile hamburger drawer + dashboard login flow + all new CSS classes (section-divider, decorative-border, img-zoom, btn-vintage, hero-bg) all working perfectly.

critical.issue: Logout only deletes session when session_token COOKIE is sent; ignores Authorization: Bearer header. Frontend stores token in localStorage and sends it as Bearer, so calling /api/auth/logout from the dashboard does NOT remove the token from MongoDB admin_sessions. Token remains valid and /api/auth/verify still returns 200 after logout. Server.py line 484: `async def logout(response: Response, session_token: str = Cookie(None))` — needs to also accept `authorization: str = Header(None)` and delete by either source.

minor.issue: Returns 200 even when called with no token / invalid token. Acceptable for idempotent logout but worth noting.
When called with no body, returns 422 (Pydantic validation) before auth check. Functionally still blocked but prefer 401 first. Low priority.

integration_issues.issue: Clicking Logout in dashboard clears localStorage on client but the MongoDB session is NOT deleted (see backend bug above). If the same token were captured/replayed, it would still work for 24h. Server-side fix required.

action_items: Fix /api/auth/logout to also accept Authorization header (Bearer token) and delete the session from db.admin_sessions, mirroring verify_session's token-resolution logic. After fix, re-run TestLogout.test_logout_invalidates_token in /app/backend/tests/test_cleanup_p0_p1.py.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py 484-489: logout() only consults the cookie. Mirror verify_session()'s dual-source token resolution (Bearer header OR cookie) before db.admin_sessions.delete_one().
server.py is 1089 lines — exceeds 700-line guideline. Consider splitting into routers (auth, cms, loyalty, messaging, giveaway, analytics) for maintainability. Not blocking.
POST /api/specials and POST /api/messages/send accept body before checking auth, leaking a 422 schema error to unauthenticated callers. Low priority but consider auth-first ordering.

test_credentials.auth_method: JWT Bearer token via POST /api/auth/login, also set as session_token httpOnly cookie

seed_data_creation: Reused existing test data from previous iterations (TEST_* loyalty members, newsletter subscribers, catering inquiries). New cleanup tests create one short-lived session per test that is left to expire naturally (24h TTL).

P1 session persistence verified: login → restart backend via supervisorctl → token still valid via MongoDB admin_sessions lookup. Mobile hamburger menu (testid mobile-menu-toggle / mobile-menu-drawer) opens, lists nav-about-mobile/nav-specials-mobile/nav-menu-mobile/nav-contact-mobile/nav-call-btn-mobile, and closes after link click. ONLY OUTSTANDING ISSUE: POST /api/auth/logout does not honour Bearer token — fix server.py logout() to accept Authorization header in addition to cookie.
rca of the issue: Bug RCA — /api/auth/logout: verify_session() at server.py:339 correctly accepts both Bearer header and session_token cookie. logout() at server.py:483-489 only declares `session_token: str = Cookie(None)` and never inspects the Authorization header, so Bearer-only callers (the React dashboard) can't invalidate sessions. Reproduction: 1) POST /api/auth/login → token. 2) POST /api/auth/logout with header `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (no cookie) → 200 returned but db.admin_sessions row remains. 3) GET /api/auth/verify with same Bearer token → 200 (still authenticated). Mitigation: change signature to `async def logout(response: Response, authorization: str = Header(None), session_token: str = Cookie(None))` and resolve token using the same Bearer-or-Cookie precedence as verify_session before calling db.admin_sessions.delete_one({'token': token}).
